heading: How it works
exactSourceText: An assay sees only the genome copies put into it (see [limit of detection and sampling](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/liquid-biopsy/limit-of-detection-and-sampling)). In the breast-cancer study below, a standard input was 4,500 genome copies of cell-free DNA (cfDNA), about 15 nanograms. At a tumor fraction of 1 in 100,000, any single tumor position is then usually absent by chance. Each additional tumor-specific variant is another, largely independent chance to catch a tumor fragment. The study's theoretical detection limit was 1 ÷ (input copies × variants tracked): with 4,500 copies and 47 variants, 1 in 211,500, or 4.7 parts per million. Knowing the exact variants also lets the assay ignore everything else, which lowers background error. Whole-genome designs push the same logic further, integrating thousands of tumor mutations to reach tumor fractions near 1 in 100,000 ([Zviran 2020](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-020-0915-3)).

heading: How it works
exactSourceText: **The general pattern, with a source.** In serial plasma from people with breast cancer, Santonja and colleagues ran tumor-informed and tumor-naive assays on the same samples. Tumor-informed assays were the most sensitive at low ctDNA levels. Hybrid-capture sequencing of 1,347 to 7,491 tumor-identified mutations per patient detected ctDNA down to an allele fraction of 2.4 parts per million (0.00024%); multiplex PCR across 21 to 47 tumor structural variants reached 4.7 parts per million ([Santonja 2023](https://doi.org/10.15252/emmm.202216505)).

The answer is only as specific as the thing added back.

heading: Upstream or downstream of the block?
exactSourceText: Think of water pipes. Closing a valve stops the flow only if the leak is downstream of the valve. If the leak is past the valve, closing it does nothing. The analogy has a limit: real pathways branch and feed back, so "downstream" must be tested, not just read from a diagram.

heading: From model to person: the safety test
exactSourceText: IACS-010759 then entered two phase 1 trials, in acute myeloid leukemia (17 people) and advanced solid tumors (23 people). Normal tissues also respire, so an energy dependence in a tumor model has to clear a toxicity test that a culture cannot run.
